svg.text: FIG 05: MILLMAN'S THEOREM, DUAL MILLMAN & MULTI-BRANCH REDUCTION ARCHITECTURE
Parallel Voltage Sources • Series Current Sources • Unbalanced Neutral Shift • Multi-Phase Star-Delta Generator Equivalences

g.text: 1. Classical Millman's Theorem
Statement: Parallel Voltage Source Branches
When N parallel branches each consisting of an ideal voltage source V_k in series
with internal resistance R_k (conductance G_k = 1/R_k) are connected across two
common bus terminals A-B, the entire bank can be reduced to a single equivalent
Thévenin generator (V_M in series with R_M):
Rigorous Nodal Derivation
Choose common terminal B as datum reference (V_B = 0 V). Let V_A = V_M.
Applying KCL at node A (sum of currents leaving node A equals zero):
V_M = [ V₁G₁ + V₂G₂ + ... + V_NG_N ] / [ G₁ + G₂ + ... + G_N ]
• Equivalent resistance: Deactivating all sources leaves G_k in parallel:
G_M = G₁ + G₂ + ... + G_N ⟹ R_M = 1 / G_M (Q.E.D.)
Source Polarity & Pure Resistor Branches
1. Polarity Sign Rule:
• If positive terminal of V_k faces node A: V_k is POSITIVE (+V_k).
• If negative terminal faces node A: V_k is NEGATIVE (-V_k).
V_M = (V₁G₁ - V₂G₂ + V₃G₃) / (G₁ + G₂ + G₃)
2. Branch with Resistor Only (Zero Voltage Source):
• For a branch with only resistor R_p: treat as V_p = 0 V!
• The term V_p · G_p = 0 in numerator, BUT G_p MUST BE INCLUDED in denominator!
Denominator = G₁ + G₂ + ... + G_p (Includes pure resistors!)
Exam Trap: Forgetting G_p in denominator gives 100% wrong voltage!
3-Branch Millman Solved Example
Parallel branches: Branch 1 (10 V, 2 Ω), Branch 2 (-20 V, 4 Ω), Branch 3 (5 Ω only):
• Millman solved this 3-loop active bridge in 20 seconds!
• Connecting any external load R_L across A-B results in load current I_L = 0 A.
Immediate inspection power: V₁G₁ balances V₂G₂!
2. Dual Millman's Theorem
Dual Statement: Series Current Source Loops
When N loops each consisting of an ideal current source I_k in parallel with
internal resistance R_k are connected in series across terminals A-B, the entire
chain collapses to a single Norton generator (I_M in parallel with R_M):
Duality Transformation Mechanics
Dual Millman is derived by applying Thévenin-Norton source transformation to each
parallel Norton cell, placing them in series, then converting back:
1. Convert each cell to Thévenin:
V_k = I_k · R_k (in series with R_k)
2. Sum Series Voltage Sources & Resistances:
V_total = ∑ (I_k · R_k) and R_total = ∑ R_k
3. Convert Series Equivalent back to Norton:
I_M = V_total / R_total = [ ∑ I_k R_k ] / [ ∑ R_k ] (Q.E.D.)
Current Source Branches in Classical Millman
What if a Classical Millman circuit contains an IDEAL CURRENT SOURCE branch?
• An ideal current source I_s entering node A has internal resistance R = ∞ Ω.
• Conductance G_s = 1/∞ = 0 S!
Modified Classical Millman Equation:
V_M = [ ∑ (V_k · G_k) + I_s,entering ] / [ ∑ G_k ]
• The current source I_s is added DIRECTLY to the numerator (since I = V·G)!
• In the denominator, it adds 0 S (conductance is zero).
Exam Super-Shortcut: Eliminates need for source transformation before Millman!

3. 3-Phase Neutral Displacement
The Neutral Shift Principle in Star-Star Networks
In a 3-phase 3-wire star-connected system without neutral wire, an unbalanced load
(Y_a ≠ Y_b ≠ Y_c) causes the load neutral n' to shift away from source neutral n.
Millman's Neutral Displacement Formula:
V_{n'n} = [ V_{an} · Y_a + V_{bn} · Y_b + V_{cn} · Y_c ] / [ Y_a + Y_b + Y_c ]
• V_{n'n} is the displacement voltage between star neutral points.
• If load is balanced (Y_a = Y_b = Y_c = Y): V_{n'n} = Y·(V_{an}+V_{bn}+V_{cn})/(3Y) = 0 V!
Actual Phase Voltages Across Unbalanced Load Arms
Once neutral displacement V_{n'n} is calculated via Millman's formula:
Load Arm Phase Voltages:
V_{an'} = V_{an} - V_{n'n}
V_{bn'} = V_{bn} - V_{n'n}
V_{cn'} = V_{cn} - V_{n'n}
Load Phase Currents:
I_a = V_{an'} · Y_a = (V_{an} - V_{n'n}) · Y_a
I_b = V_{bn'} · Y_b = (V_{bn} - V_{n'n}) · Y_b
I_c = V_{cn'} · Y_c = (V_{cn} - V_{n'n}) · Y_c
4-Wire System with Finite Neutral Impedance Z_n
If a physical neutral conductor connects neutrals n and n' with impedance Z_n:
• Treat neutral conductor as a 4th branch with source V_n = 0 V and admittance Y_n = 1/Z_n!
Generalized 4th-Wire Millman Equation:
V_{n'n} = [ V_{an}Y_a + V_{bn}Y_b + V_{cn}Y_c ] / [ Y_a + Y_b + Y_c + Y_n ]
• Solid Neutral Wire (Z_n = 0 ⟹ Y_n → ∞): V_{n'n} = 0 V (Zero neutral shift!).
• Broken Neutral Wire (Open Circuit ⟹ Y_n = 0): Maximum dangerous neutral shift!
Power System Hazard: Broken neutral over-voltages blow single-phase appliances!
3-Phase Classroom Numerical Drill
Unbalanced loads: Phase a has R = 10 Ω (Y_a = 0.1 S); Phases b & c are open (Y_b=Y_c=0):
Phase a load voltage:
• Load neutral floats completely up to Phase a voltage!
• Voltage between phase b and load neutral: V_{bn'} = 100∠-120° - 100∠0° = 173.2 V (Line-to-Line)!
Millman provides instantaneous physical visualization of floating star points!
4. Reductions & Equivalences
Delta-Star (Δ ↔ Y) Conversion Formulas
Delta to Star (Δ → Y) Conversion:
R_a = (R_{ab} · R_{ca}) / (R_{ab} + R_{bc} + R_{ca})
Mnemonic: Product of Adjacent Delta Sides / Perimeter Sum of all 3 Sides
Star to Delta (Y → Δ) Conversion:
R_{ab} = R_a + R_b + (R_a · R_b) / R_c
Mnemonic: Sum of Pairwise Products / Opposite Star Arm Resistance
Symmetrical Case (Equal Resistors R): R_Y = R_Δ / 3 and R_Δ = 3 · R_Y
THE CAPACITOR Δ ↔ Y INVERSION TRAP
The #1 formula memory error in competitive exams!
Because impedance is INVERSE to capacitance (Z_C = 1 / sC):
For Capacitors: C_Y = 3 · C_Δ (MULTIPLY by 3!)
C_Δ = C_Y / 3 (DIVIDE by 3!)
Memory Contrast Matrix:
• Resistors & Inductors: R_Y = R_Δ / 3 and L_Y = L_Δ / 3
• Capacitors (Inverted): C_Y = 3 · C_Δ (Capacitance in Star is LARGER!)
Source Shift Theorems (Blakesley's Theorems)
1. Voltage Source Shift Through a Node:
• A voltage source V_s connected in one branch connected to a node can be
shifted through the node by placing identical voltage sources V_s in series
with ALL OTHER branches connected to that node (pointing away from node)!
2. Current Source Shift Around a Loop:
• A current source I_s bridging two distant nodes can be shifted through
intermediate nodes by creating a loop of identical current sources I_s!
Benefit: Eliminates floating sources without creating supernodes or supermeshes!
Master Reduction Decision Tree
Can branches be combined in series or parallel directly?
YES ⟹ Apply standard R_eq = R₁ + R₂ or R₁ ∥ R₂.
Are multiple voltage sources in parallel sharing 2 common buses?
YES ⟹ Use Millman's Theorem: V_M = ∑(V_k G_k) / ∑ G_k.
Is network a closed bridge or triangular mesh?
YES ⟹ Apply Delta-Star (Δ ↔ Y) transformation.
Are sources floating across non-reference nodes?
YES ⟹ Apply Source Shift or Supernode/Supermesh method.
Systematic reduction eliminates 80% of equation solving time!
